title: deployment-architecture-option-set.json
content:
Purpose
This working doc summarizes alternative deployment architectures (hosted, dedicated, private) for customer POCs and provides a recommended phased POC approach with test criteria, decision matrix, and implementation notes. Audience: SEs, solutions architects, prospect engineering leads.

Customer context (example prospect: FinData Corp)
- Use case: document summarization + customer support assistant; latency targets: <300ms p50 for short queries, throughput ~120 qps during peak; data residency: EU-only; compliance: SOC2 + encryption at rest + audit logging.
- Constraints: budget-conscious, prefers consumption pricing but may accept reserved capacity for predictable latency.
- Timeline: 6 week exec timeline: 2 week POC, 4 week pilot.

High-level options overview
1) Hosted API (Redwood-managed cloud endpoints)
   - Pros: fastest onboarding, minimal infra work, bursting capacity, immediate telemetry in Console. Good for evaluating functional fit and latency for non-sensitive traffic.
   - Cons: data leaves customer network unless configured with Private networking add-ons; limited network controls; potential cost variability.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity in Redwood tenancy)
   - Pros: predictable throughput, isolated GPU pool (logical isolation), SLA-backed latency, simpler ramp from hosted; optional VPC peering.
   - Cons: commitment required; longer lead time to spin up capacity; still runs in Redwood-managed infra (not customer-owned).

3) Private (VPC / on-prem)
   - Pros: full network control, suitable for regulated/data-sensitive workloads, supports air-gapped on-prem installs.
   - Cons: longest lead time, ops burden for customer or Redwood in private deployment model, potential feature parity lag depending on release cadence.

Decision criteria (shortlist)
- Latency (p50/p95),
- Throughput / concurrency,
- Data residency & egress controls,
- Cost predictability,
- Time-to-proof (onboard speed),
- Operational burden for customer,
- Compliance (audit logs, KMS integration).

Lightweight decision matrix (scores: 1=weak,5=strong)
- Hosted: Latency 3, Throughput 4, Residency 2, Cost predictability 2, Time-to-proof 5, Ops burden 1, Compliance 2.
- Dedicated: Latency 4, Throughput 5, Residency 3, Cost predictability 4, Time-to-proof 3, Ops burden 2, Compliance 3.
- Private: Latency 4, Throughput 4, Residency 5, Cost predictability 3, Time-to-proof 2, Ops burden 4, Compliance 5.
(Use this shorthand to align with customer priorities; weights vary by customer.)

Recommended POC approach (phased, hybrid-friendly)
Phase 0: Pre-POC alignment (3–5 days)
- Technical kickoff with customer infra and security teams. Capture network topology, KMS, compliance checklist, and desired dataset for eval.
- Deliverables: Scope doc, success criteria (latency, accuracy, token cost), SLA expectations, contact matrix.

Phase 1: Hosted functional POC (7–10 days)
Goal: validate model quality, prompt design, and integration patterns with minimal friction.
- Provision hosted API endpoint, test dataset ingestion (synthetic + redacted real examples), run scripted evals (ROUGE/F1 where applicable), and collect quality/latency stats.
- Telemetry: use Console traces, token breakdown, sample logs.
- Success criteria: baseline accuracy within X% of target, p50 latency <300ms for short prompts in EU region, integration end-to-end.
Why start hosted: fastest path to show value, reduces risk for customer sign-off, and gives concrete numbers for capacity planning.

Phase 2: Capacity & compliance validation (10–14 days) — Dedicated or Private depending on alignment
Option A — Dedicated preview
- Provision a temporary dedicated pool sized to expected pilot throughput (e.g., 2x expected qps to test autoscaling behaviour).
- Validate autoscaling, routing policies, KV/prefix cache effectiveness, and cost/run-rate estimates under load.
- Test canary rollout and fallback policies between model variants.
Option B — Private preview (VPC or on-prem staging)
- Set up Private control plane with customer VPC peering and test end-to-end network flows, KMS integration, and audit logs retention.
- Run compliance checklist: ensure encryption-at-rest with customer KMS, verify access logs, and run a simple penetration/light-scan with security team.
Deliverables: load test report, security checklist sign-off, cost projection for pilot.

Phase 3: Pilot (2–4 weeks)
- Decide: Dedicated vs Private for pilot based on Phase 2. Deploy pilot integration to subset of traffic (canary 5–10%). Collect production-like metrics: latency SLO conformance, error rates, cost per 1k tokens, and user satisfaction metrics.
- Execute rollback plans and incident runbooks.
Success criteria: stable SLOs under expected load, no compliance-critical failures, executive OK to proceed to contract.

Implementation notes and ops playbook (practical items)
- Networking: for VPC peering test, exchange CIDR ranges early; provide Terraform snippet for peering and route table entries.
- KMS: exchange KMS key arn and validate role permissions. Include a stub IAM policy in repo.
- Model version pinning: recommend pinning to a 2-week stable model for pilot and enable automatic fallback to a smaller quantized variant for degradation scenarios.
- Logging: ensure sample retention policy is set for audit windows; provide obfuscation script for PII in sample logs.
- Cost controls: set per-route token caps and alerting for burst spend; estimate token burn in hosted POC and compare to Dedicated reservation sizing.

Sample risk register
- Risk: Hosted POC shows latency variance due to noisy neighbor. Mitigation: move to temporary Dedicated preview; enable smaller quantized model to meet latency.
- Risk: KMS integration delays. Mitigation: run an offline KMS smoke test with a stub key earlier in Phase 0.
- Risk: Feature parity gap when using Private on older runtime. Mitigation: document required runtime features and include upgrade plan.

POC success metrics (concrete)
- Quality: task-specific metric (e.g., extractive F1 >= 0.72; user satisfaction NPS >= 6 among pilot users)
- Latency: p50 < 300ms, p95 < 700ms for short prompts in EU region
- Reliability: error rate < 0.5% over 48h rolling window
- Cost: projected token cost per 1k interactions within budget target +/- 15%

Open questions for customer (to resolve during kickoff)
- Is there an absolute requirement for customer-managed keys, or is Redwood-managed KMS acceptable for POC?
- Are there IP/ML model audit requirements (e.g., must not send gradients or derived embeddings back to Redwood)?
- What is the SLA/uptime expectation for pilot (0, 99.9, 99.95)?
- Any blacklisted third-party services or restricted outbound endpoints?

Next steps / action items
- SEs: schedule technical kickoff and invite security + infra (owner: Mateo Chen, due: 2025-01-20).
- Solutions Eng: prepare Terraform peering snippets and KMS IAM policy template (owner: Lila Thompson, due: 2025-01-22).
- Sales: confirm budget guardrails and pilot duration with procurement (owner: Ethan Park, due: 2025-01-17).
- Ops: provision temporary dedicated pool estimate for capacity testing (owner: Aisha Kapoor, due: 2025-01-28).

Notes / shorthand logs (team scratchpad)
- Quick wins: start with hosted to unblock product evaluation.
- Keep customer in loop on fallback options: show how Dedicated -> Private migration flows work with minimal code changes (same API, different endpoint).
- TODO: draft customer-facing 1-pager summarizing phases and responsibilities.

Appendix: quick checklist for SE demo run
- Register account in EU region; spin up hosted endpoint and run 50 query smoke test.
- Run token usage estimate script and attach to proposal.
- Build minimal integration sample (serverless function) to show start-to-finish from web UI to Redwood response.

References
- Confluence: POC checklist (linked above), Dedicated sizing guide, Private deployment checklist.
- GitHub: prod-deploy-playbooks PR #78 (linked above)

End of draft.
